tasks.title: Essay – traffic in city centres
tasks.prompt:
Your class has watched a documentary about ways of reducing traffic in city centres. You have made the notes below.

Ways of reducing traffic:
• congestion charges
• better public transport
• car-free zones

Some opinions expressed in the documentary:
“Charging drivers just hits people on low incomes.”
“Nobody will leave their car at home if the buses are always late.”
“Streets without cars feel completely different.”

Write an essay discussing two of the ways in your notes. You should explain which way is more effective, giving reasons to support your opinion.

You may, if you wish, make use of the opinions expressed in the documentary, but you should use your own words as far as possible.
points: Wyraźny wybór, który jest skuteczniejszy, z uzasadnieniem
Opinie z polecenia sparafrazowane, nie przepisane
tasks.model:
Few city dwellers would deny that congestion has become one of the defining frustrations of modern urban life. Among the measures proposed to tackle it, congestion charges and improved public transport attract the most attention, yet they differ considerably in both fairness and effectiveness.

Charging drivers to enter the centre has undoubtedly reduced traffic in cities such as London, and the revenue can be reinvested in the transport network. Critics, however, argue that such a policy penalises those on low incomes, who may have no alternative to driving and can least afford the charge. Were the charge to be set too high, it could also drive shoppers and businesses away from the centre altogether.

Better public transport, by contrast, offers an incentive rather than a penalty. Not only does a punctual, frequent and affordable service give commuters a genuine reason to leave their cars at home, but it also benefits those who cannot drive at all. Even a generous incentive will fail to move drivers if services run unreliably, which is why reliability matters more than novelty.

On balance, I would argue that investment in public transport is the more effective strategy, since it solves the underlying problem rather than merely discouraging its symptoms. Charges may play a useful supporting role, but only once a credible alternative exists. Until then, asking people to pay for the privilege of having no choice is unlikely to win public support.

summary: Esej omawia dwa z trzech sposobów z notatek (opłaty i transport publiczny), a czytelnik od razu widzi kryteria porównania: sprawiedliwość i skuteczność.
Cytowane w poleceniu opinie są sparafrazowane, a nie przepisane, i wplecione w argumentację.
Wybór jest jasny i uzasadniony: transport publiczny rozwiązuje przyczynę, a opłaty mają co najwyżej rolę wspierającą.
Język C1: inwersja warunkowa, Not only does…, przysłówki oceniające i formalne łączniki bez nadmiaru ozdobników.
Najsłabszym miejscem jest niedopracowany argument za opłatami – autor wspomina o wpływach, ale ich nie rozwija.

tasks.title: Essay – preparing young people for work
tasks.prompt:
Your class has attended a panel discussion about how schools can prepare young people for working life. You have made the notes below.

Ways schools can prepare young people for work:
• work experience placements
• teaching practical skills
• careers advice

Some opinions expressed in the discussion:
“Two weeks in an office teaches you more than a year in a classroom.”
“Most school leavers can't manage their own money.”
“Advisers often know very little about today's job market.”

Write an essay discussing two of the ways in your notes. You should explain which way is more important for schools to focus on, giving reasons to support your opinion.

You may, if you wish, make use of the opinions expressed in the discussion, but you should use your own words as far as possible.
points: Wyraźny wybór, który jest ważniejszy, z uzasadnieniem
Opinie z polecenia sparafrazowane, nie przepisane
tasks.model:
It is often claimed that schools concentrate so heavily on examinations that pupils leave without the faintest idea of how the working world operates. Of the various remedies suggested, work experience placements and the teaching of practical skills are arguably the most promising, though their merits are not identical.

Placements give teenagers a first-hand glimpse of professional life. Spending a fortnight in an office or a workshop can reveal what a particular career actually involves, and it often builds confidence that no textbook can provide. Nevertheless, the quality of such placements varies enormously: a student who spends two weeks making tea and photocopying documents will learn very little, and the experience is, in any case, short-lived.

Practical skills, on the other hand, stay with a person for decades. Learning to budget, to fill in a tax form or to read a payslip is not glamorous, yet it equips young people for the realities of adult life, whatever profession they eventually choose. It is worrying that so many school leavers are unable to manage their own money, and it is hardly surprising that debt problems follow.

Taking everything into account, I would contend that schools should give priority to practical skills. Not only are they useful in every career, but they can also be taught to an entire class at minimal cost, whereas placements depend on the goodwill of local employers. Ideally, the two should complement one another, with placements allowing pupils to apply what they have learnt.

Wybór jest jasny i uzasadniony: umiejętności praktyczne są użyteczne w każdej karierze i tańsze do nauczenia.
Opinie z polecenia zostały sparafrazowane, a nie przepisane (np. unable to manage their own money).

tasks.title: Proposal – staff wellbeing
tasks.prompt:
The company you work for wants to improve the wellbeing of its staff and has invited employees to send in proposals. Write a proposal describing the main problems affecting staff at the moment, suggesting two or three changes the company could make, and explaining how these changes would benefit both the staff and the company.

Write your proposal.
tasks.model:
Proposal: Improving Staff Wellbeing

Introduction
This proposal outlines the main factors currently affecting the wellbeing of our staff and suggests three changes which would benefit both employees and the company.

Current problems
Following informal conversations with colleagues, it became clear that two issues cause the greatest concern. Firstly, many people work long hours at their desks without a proper break, and complain of headaches and tiredness by the afternoon. Secondly, those who live far from the office spend up to two hours commuting, which leaves very little time for family or leisure.

Suggested changes
I would suggest introducing a lunchtime break of at least forty-five minutes, away from the desk, in a quiet room equipped with comfortable seating. In addition, the company could offer flexible working hours, allowing employees to start and finish earlier or later to avoid the rush hour. A third option would be to allow staff to work from home one day a week, provided that their duties permit it.

Expected benefits
Staff would undoubtedly feel more relaxed and motivated, and they would be able to spend more time with their families. The company, for its part, would benefit from fewer sick days, higher productivity and an improved reputation, which would help to attract talented candidates. The cost of these changes would be minimal, whereas the potential gains are considerable.

summary: Propozycja ma tytuł, nagłówki i cztery wymagane elementy: problemy, zmiany, korzyści dla pracowników i dla firmy.
Ton jest przekonujący i grzeczny (I would suggest, the company could), a kolejność porządkują proste wskaźniki (Firstly, Secondly, In addition).
Każda rekomendacja jest konkretna: czas przerwy, elastyczne godziny, jeden dzień pracy zdalnej.
Zakres językowy podnoszą konstrukcje warunkowe (provided that) i zdania względne z which.
Argument finansowy jest jednak zbyt ogólny – autor twierdzi, że koszt jest minimalny, ale tego nie wyjaśnia.

tasks.title: Report – international festival
tasks.prompt:
You helped to organise an international festival at your college last month. The principal has asked you to write a report. In your report you should evaluate how successful the festival was, describe any problems that occurred, and recommend improvements for next year's festival.

Write your report.
points: Ocena, na ile festiwal był udany
genreChecklist: Tytuł, nagłówki i wstęp z celem raportu
Bezosobowy styl (passive, It is recommended that)
tasks.model:
Report on the International Festival

Introduction
The purpose of this report is to evaluate last month's International Festival, to outline the difficulties that arose and to make recommendations for next year's event. The findings are based on my own experience as a member of the organising committee and on feedback from participants.

Overall success
On the whole, the festival was a considerable success. Attendance exceeded expectations, with more than 800 visitors over the two days, and the food stalls and dance performances were particularly well received. Students from fourteen countries took part, which gave the event a truly international character. It is also worth noting that the profits donated to a local charity were higher than anticipated.

Problems encountered
Two main problems should be mentioned. Firstly, the sound system failed during the opening ceremony, causing a delay of almost forty minutes. Secondly, the main hall became overcrowded in the afternoon, and several visitors left because they could not find a seat. Volunteers were not clearly identifiable, which made it difficult for newcomers to obtain help.

Recommendations
Next year, it is recommended that the sound equipment be tested the day before the event. Furthermore, the programme could be spread across two venues in order to relieve the pressure on the main hall. Finally, volunteers should be provided with brightly coloured T-shirts so that visitors can recognise them easily. If these measures are adopted, next year's festival should run more smoothly and attract an even wider audience.

summary: Raport ma tytuł, wstęp z celem i osobne sekcje: ocena, problemy, rekomendacje – dokładnie trzy elementy polecenia.
Styl jest bezosobowy i rzeczowy (passive, it is recommended that), a rekomendacje są w osobnej, jasno opisanej sekcji.
Autor podaje konkrety: liczbę gości, liczbę krajów, opóźnienie o prawie czterdzieści minut.
Język C1 widać w strukturach z trybem łączącym (be tested) i w zdaniach względnych odnoszących się do całej myśli.
Źródło „feedbacku uczestników” jest wspomniane, ale nigdzie nie ma jego wyniku.

tasks.title: Review – a learning app
tasks.prompt:
You see this announcement on an education website:

“Has an app or online service changed the way you learn something? Write a review telling us what it is, evaluating its strengths and weaknesses, and explaining what kind of people would benefit most from using it.”

Write your review.
tasks.model:
Learning a language in ten minutes a day? Lingua Loop reviewed

When I downloaded Lingua Loop, a language-learning app, eighteen months ago, I was sceptical. Having failed to stick to every evening class I had ever joined, I doubted that a smartphone app could succeed where teachers had not. Yet it has changed the way I study Spanish more than I could have imagined.

What sets the app apart is its short, game-like lessons, each of which takes roughly ten minutes. Not only do they fit easily into a busy day, but the daily streak counter also creates a gentle pressure that keeps users coming back. The spaced-repetition system, which reminds you of words just before you are likely to forget them, is another genuine strength, and my vocabulary has grown steadily as a result.

That said, the app is far from perfect. Grammar explanations are minimal, so learners who want to understand why a sentence is built in a particular way are left to search elsewhere. Moreover, the speaking exercises rely on voice recognition, which sometimes misinterprets perfectly good pronunciation and can be maddening.

All in all, I would recommend Lingua Loop to beginners and busy people who need a regular, low-effort habit. Those aiming at fluency, however, would do well to combine it with conversation practice and a good grammar book. For me, it has been the missing first step.

summary: Recenzja podaje, czym jest aplikacja, ocenia mocne i słabe strony oraz mówi, dla kogo jest najlepsza – wszystkie trzy elementy polecenia.
